The '''1965–66 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|63rd season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|34th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
The club remained at first place almost the entire campaign before was defeated 1–2 by [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]] and lost the title against local rivals [[Atlético Madrid]] one round before season finale<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Diario Marca|title=La flor del Real Madrid Yé-yé|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/07/07/futbol/mas_futbol/1310030818.html?a=d4b430a7096e9c1309423dd461d4cc04&t=1354897168|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> by just one single point.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/especiales/2002/02/centenario/1955.html |title=Historia del Real Madrid, 100 años uno a uno|publisher=Diario El Mundo|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> [[UD Levante]] defender [[Antonio Calpe]] arrived to enforce the back-up, also, [[CD Málaga]] midfielder [[Manuel Velázquez]] returned from a two years loan replacing French playmaker [[Lucien Muller]],<ref>Transferred out to FC Barcelona</ref> also, transferred in was defender [[Pedro de Felipe]]<ref>[http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1969/09/15/pagina-3/950452/pdf.html Bustillo, tres meses de inactividad (Bustillo, three months out)]; [[Mundo Deportivo]], 17 September 1969 {{in lang|es}}</ref> from [[Rayo Vallecano]] benching [[José Emilio Santamaría|José Santamaría]] both arrivals featured a superb season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/realmadrid-in-ec.html|title=Real Madrid CF – All the players in European Cups|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|accessdate=18 January 2020}}</ref>

Meanwhile, in [[1965–66 European Cup|European Cup]] the squad clinched its sixth trophy after defeated [[Inter Milan|Inter]] in Semi-finals and on 11 May 1966 won 2–1 the [[1966 European Cup Final|Final]] against [[Abdulah Gegic]]' [[FK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] which, previously, in semi-finals eliminated heavily favourites [[Manchester United]] without star [[George Best]].<ref>{{cite book |language=French |publisher=L'équipe |title=Football 50 ans de coupes d'Europe |author=Hachette, Issy-les-Moulineaux|page=62, un real Madrid nouvelle vague |isbn=2-9519605-9-X}}</ref> Three days after the Final, the [[Yé-yé (Real Madrid)|Yé-yé]] team was introduced to the world after 4 players posed for ''Diario Marca'' as then popular English rock band [[The Beatles]] resulting in the nickname from their theme song <<[[She Loves You]]>> chorus hit "Yeah-yeah".<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Diario Marca|title=La flor del Real Madrid Yé-yé|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/07/07/futbol/mas_futbol/1310030818.html?a=d4b430a7096e9c1309423dd461d4cc04&t=1354897168|access-date=7 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622091902/https://www.marca.com/2011/07/07/futbol/mas_futbol/1310030818.html?a=d4b430a7096e9c1309423dd461d4cc04&t=1354897168|archive-date=22 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the [[1966 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]], Madrid was eliminated by [[Real Betis]] in the quarter-finals 5–4 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/01/18/mas_futbol/1137569212_850215.html|title=El Betis de Londa noquea al Madrid Yé-Yé|publisher=as.com|language=Spanish}}</ref> After seven seasons, 5 League titles and 3 European Cup trophies,<ref>Puskas did not play the 1959 and 1966 Finals</ref> Hungarian forward [[Ferenc Puskás]] left the club during the summer.
